**Hydrogen – A Quick Reference Guide to Its Properties**

| Category | Property | Value / Description |
|----------|----------|---------------------|
| **Basic Atomic Data** | Atomic number | 1 |
| | Atomic mass (average) | 1.008 u |
| | Electron configuration | 1s¹ |
| | Isotopes | ¹H (protium, 99.98 %), ²H (deuterium, 0.02 %), ³H (tritium, trace) |
| | Ionization energy | 13.598 eV (first) |
| | Electron affinity | –0.754 eV (negative, so H⁻ is unstable in gas phase) |
| | Electronegativity (Pauling) | 2.20 |
| | Atomic radius | ~31 pm (covalent) |
| | Van der Waals radius | ~120 pm |
| **Physical State (at 25 °C, 1 atm)** | State | Gas |
| | Density | 0.08988 g L⁻¹ |
| | Molar volume | 22.414 L mol⁻¹ |
| | Boiling point | –252.87 °C (−423.17 °F) |
| | Melting point | –259.16 °C (−434.49 °F) |
| | Specific heat (gas, 1 bar) | 14.304 J g⁻¹ K⁻¹ |
| | Thermal conductivity | 0.180 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹ |
| | Speed of sound | 1270 m s⁻¹ |
| | Refractive index | 1.000132 (visible light) |
| **Chemical Properties** | Oxidation states | +1 (most common), –1 (hydride), 0 (elemental) |
| | Common compounds | H₂O, H₂SO₄, HCl, NH₃, CH₄, H₂O₂, etc. |
| | Bond dissociation energy (H–H) | 436 kJ mol⁻¹ |
| | Standard enthalpy of formation (H₂(g)) | 0 kJ mol⁻¹ (by definition) |
| | Standard Gibbs free energy of formation (H₂(g)) | 0 kJ mol⁻¹ |
| | Standard entropy (H₂(g)) | 130.68 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ |
| | pKa of H₃O⁺ | –1.74 (in water) |
| | pKa of H₂O | 15.7 (in water) |
| | Redox potential (H⁺/H₂) | 0 V (vs SHE) |
| | Solubility in water | 1.6 g L⁻¹ at 25 °C (≈0.0006 mol L⁻¹) |
| | Solubility in organic solvents | Very low (except in supercritical CO₂) |
| **Isotopic Variants** | Deuterium (²H) | 2.014 u; heavier, lower zero‑point energy → stronger bonds, higher boiling/melting points |
| | Tritium (³H) | 3.016 u; radioactive (β⁻ decay, half‑life ≈12.32 y) |
| | Applications | Deuterium used in heavy water reactors, NMR spectroscopy; tritium used in nuclear fusion research and luminous paints |
| **Spectroscopic Features** | Rotational constant (H₂) | 59.3 cm⁻¹ |
| | Vibrational frequency (H₂) | 4401 cm⁻¹ |
| | Ionization potential (H₂⁺) | 24.6 eV |
| | UV absorption (H₂) | Lyman series (121.6 nm) |
| **Thermodynamic Data** | Standard enthalpy of formation (H₂O(l)) | –285.83 kJ mol⁻¹ |
| | Standard enthalpy of formation (H₂O(g)) | –241.82 kJ mol⁻¹ |
| | Standard Gibbs free energy of formation (H₂O(l)) | –237.13 kJ mol⁻¹ |
| | Standard Gibbs free energy of formation (H₂O(g)) | –228.57 kJ mol⁻¹ |
| **Miscellaneous** | Magnetic moment | 1 µB (electron spin) |
| | Nuclear spin | ½ (¹H), 1 (²H), ½ (³H) |
| | Proton mass | 1.007276 u |
| | Neutron mass | 1.008665 u |
| | Binding energy per nucleon (¹H) | 0 MeV (no binding) |
| | Role in stars | Fusion of H into He powers the Sun; H‑burning via proton‑proton chain or CNO cycle |
| | Environmental impact | Hydrogen combustion produces only water; however, large‑scale production often relies on fossil fuels (CO₂ emissions) |

---

### Quick Takeaways

1. **Lightest element** – Hydrogen is the simplest atom, with one proton and one electron.
2. **Highly reactive** – Forms a wide variety of compounds; its +1 oxidation state dominates.
3. **Gas at STP** – Extremely low density; can be stored as a liquid under high pressure or cryogenic temperatures.
4. **Isotopic diversity** – Deuterium and tritium give rise to distinct physical and chemical behaviors.
5. **Energy carrier** – Hydrogen fuel cells produce electricity with water as the only by‑product, but the challenge lies in clean, efficient production and storage.

Feel free to ask for deeper dives into any of these categories—whether you’re curious about hydrogen’s role in astrophysics, its industrial applications, or the nuances of its isotopes!
